tasks.short: Coordinate fitting of heavy parts with other workers.

steps.what: List part number, serial and bay from the maintenance system.
Coordinate fitting and alignment of heavy parts with other workers.

tasks.design: A configured read in the {OTHER} maintenance system lists part number, serial and bay from the open work order before the lift. She still coordinates fitting and alignment with the other workers in the hangar. The list sends no message and raises no alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: The bay was often only on a paper card, and the lift depends on who is standing at the part.
tasks.enabler_now: The work order can show part number, serial and bay when a planner already filled them. No model is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Aligning a heavy part still needs the people in the hangar.
tasks.human_edge: She calls the lift and sees whether the part will actually fit.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes about who calls the lift. She spends a little less time hunting the bay.

reach.task: Set the heavy part in place during the lift.
reach.learn: Which bay and serial the work order names before the lift starts.

evidence.claim: From model knowledge, hangar crews still agree the lift in person beside the part. A work order opened earlier can already hold part number, serial and bay.
Using log timestamps to watch technician speed needs works-council consent. Annex III does not cover this work unless the logs feed a staff performance evaluation.

assumptions: The planner opens the work order before this task. Fields are part number, serial and bay. That capture is outside this task and is not counted as saved.
If any of those fields is blank, the list is empty. She reads the paper card during the hangar talk, and that talk stays at full time.
The talk with other workers is inside the organisation. It is not a document sent outside, and it is not gated.
The list does not time the lift. Upkeep of 0.2 hours per 100 baseline hours is for correcting a stale bay before the lift.
unknowns: Whether this company's work order stores part number, serial and bay as separate fields.
research_questions: How often is the bay blank on the work order at the moment of the lift?

incremental.description: Correct a bay or serial when the work order is stale before the lift.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the work order has no bay, the list is empty and the hangar talk stays as long as today. High is a week where part, serial and bay are already filled.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Count stock and requisition the short parts.

steps.what: Count supplies, parts, materials and equipment in the crib.
Name each short part number and the quantity to order.
File parts requisition v1 for the supplies she chose to order.
Check parts requisition v1 quotes only parts she named.

tasks.design: After she names each short part and quantity, the {PROCUREMENT} files parts requisition v1 and stops if a part number is unknown. She checks that version before it stands. Purchasing places any supplier order later; this task does not send one and raises no alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: The shortage judgement sat in the crib, and a wrong part number is costly to unwind.
tasks.enabler_now: A purchasing system can file a requisition from the part number and quantity she already named, and stop when the part number is unknown.
tasks.still_hard: She still has to see the bin. Purchasing still places any supplier order.
tasks.human_edge: She decides which shortage is real for the job in front of her.
tasks.altitude: She still chooses the shortage. The only standing record is parts requisition v1, and only after she checks that version.

reach.task: Place the supplier order from a checked requisition.
reach.learn: Which lines she has already checked, and that an unchecked file is not an order.

evidence.claim: From model knowledge, a mechanic in a mid-size shop counts the bin and raises an internal requisition. Purchasing places the supplier order.
Using log timestamps to watch technician speed needs works-council consent. Annex III does not cover this work unless the logs feed a staff performance evaluation.

assumptions: The stores planner maintains the part master before this task. The field used here is part number. That upkeep is outside this task and is not counted as saved.
She names part number and quantity before the file. The file copies only those lines. If a part number is not on the part master, or she names nothing, the file does not run.
When the file does not run, no version is committed. She writes today's paper note during the check step, which stays at full time. That note is not sent to a supplier.
The supplier order is the purchasing clerk's later work, not a step here. The requisition is internal. It does not time her count.
Upkeep of 0.3 hours per 100 baseline hours is for a line whose part number does not match the part master.
unknowns: Whether purchasing accepts a requisition the mechanic files, and whether bin labels match the part master.
research_questions: What share of shortages she names already have a part number purchasing knows?

incremental.description: Redo a line when the part number she named is not on the part master.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When bin labels are unreadable the file does not run and she writes the paper note. High is a week where every short part has a known part number and she only checks the filed version.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Modify aircraft structures following the drawings.

steps.what: List the drawing revision the engineering order names.
Modify aircraft structures and components following those drawings.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} shows the drawing revision the engineering order already names. She still modifies the aircraft structure or component by hand. This task does not file a release, send a message, or raise an alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: The right drawing revision was buried in a folder, and reading the drawing is the job.
tasks.enabler_now: The document store can open the revision the engineering order already names. No model reads the drawing.
tasks.still_hard: The modification is hand work on the aircraft. A wrong reading can harm people.
tasks.human_edge: She judges how to follow the drawing on this airframe.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes about who modifies the aircraft. She spends a little less time hunting the revision.

reach.task: Issue the engineering order and the drawing revision.
reach.learn: Which revision this modification is allowed to follow.

evidence.claim: From model knowledge, the mechanic still modifies the aircraft by hand while following the drawing in front of her.
EASA Part-145 keeps detailed maintenance records for 3 years from release, protected from damage, alteration and theft.

assumptions: The structures engineer files the engineering order before this task. Fields are drawing id and revision. That writing is outside this task and is not counted as saved.
If the revision is blank, the list is empty. She finds the paper drawing during the modification, which stays at full time.
No release, job card or maintenance record is filed here. The record duty stays with the task that signs the release.
Upkeep of 0.2 hours per 100 baseline hours is for chasing a missing revision before she starts.
unknowns: Whether engineering orders in this document store name a drawing revision as its own field.
research_questions: How often does the engineering order omit the drawing revision?

incremental.description: Chase a missing drawing revision before the modification starts.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the engineering order names no revision she hunts the drawing as today. High is a job where the revision is already on the order.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Make adjustments while accompanying the flight.

steps.what: List open defects for this aircraft from the technical log.
Accompany aircraft on flights and make the adjustments and corrections.

tasks.design: The technical log in the {OTHER} lists open defects already stored for this aircraft. She still accompanies the flight and makes the adjustments herself. The list does not change the log, send a message, or raise an alert.
tasks.previous_blocker: Open defects lived on a paper log that travelled with the aircraft.
tasks.enabler_now: An electronic technical log can list defects already stored. Reading them does not adjust the aircraft.
tasks.still_hard: The correction happens in flight, with people on board.
tasks.human_edge: She decides the correction while she is on the aircraft.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes about who rides the flight or who makes the correction.

reach.task: Keep the open defects on the technical log.
reach.learn: Which defect is still open before she boards.

evidence.claim: From model knowledge, the mechanic still rides the flight and makes the adjustment. A list of stored defects does not perform that correction.
A named product replaces the paper technical log on the aircraft.
In a two-month parallel run the paper process had 52 errors and the electronic log had 1. That count is not time saved on this flight.

EASA Part-145 keeps detailed maintenance records for 3 years from release, protected from damage, alteration and theft. Using log timestamps to watch technician speed needs works-council consent. Annex III does not cover this work unless the logs feed a staff performance evaluation.

assumptions: The certifying technician writes each open defect on the technical log before this task. Fields are aircraft registration and defect text. That writing is outside this task and is not counted as saved.
If the defect field is blank, the list is empty. She reads the paper log on the aircraft, and the flight stays at full time.
Telling the flight crew what she changed is talk inside the operation, not a document sent outside. Nothing is filed from this task.
The list does not time her work and does not score staff. The parallel-run error count is not used as a saving.
Upkeep of 0.2 hours per 100 baseline hours is for a defect the list could not show.
unknowns: Whether this fleet's technical log stores open defects as fields, or only as free text on paper.
research_questions: Are open defects structured on the log this fleet uses in flight?

incremental.description: Confirm a defect the list could not show because the log field was blank.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the technical log has no open-defect field she reads the paper log on the aircraft. High is a flight where those defects are already stored.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still coordinates the lift, counts the bins, modifies the aircraft, and rides the flight. Lists do not choose the lift, the shortage, the modification, or the correction.
skills_to_grow: Compare a requisition line with the part number she named.
Stop a modification when the drawing revision is missing.
Read an open defect without treating the list as the in-flight correction.
role.ambitious_version: She raises a shortage the same day the bin is short, and she refuses a requisition line she did not name. The lift, the modification, and the flight stay hers. No unchecked requisition is sent onward.
